title: Zero-Downtime Deployment Strategy
question: Design a zero-downtime deployment strategy for a Spring Boot application. Requirements: 1) No dropped requests during deployment, 2) Graceful shutdown of old instances, 3) Health check integration with load balancer, 4) Database schema migrations without downtime, 5) Rollback capability, 6) Blue-green or rolling deployment support. Discuss: enabling graceful shutdown with server.shutdown=graceful and timeout configuration, implementing /actuator/health with readiness and liveness probes, using readiness probe that returns OUT_OF_SERVICE during shutdown to signal load balancer, implementing Flyway or Liquibase with backward-compatible migrations, using expand-contract pattern for schema changes (add new column, migrate data, remove old column in next release), configuring load balancer health check interval and failure threshold, implementing connection draining period, using feature flags to toggle between old and new behavior, implementing blue-green deployment with two identical production environments, using rolling deployment with gradual traffic shifting, monitoring error rates and latency during deployment, implementing automatic rollback triggers, and testing deployment process in staging environment.

title: Optimize Application Startup Time
question: Optimize Spring Boot application startup time for faster scaling. Requirements: 1) Reduce startup time from 30s to under 10s, 2) Maintain functionality, 3) Measurable metrics, 4) Cloud-native deployment ready. Discuss: enabling lazy initialization with spring.main.lazy-initialization=true, analyzing startup time with /actuator/startup endpoint, using spring-boot-maven-plugin with optimization flags, enabling class data sharing (CDS) with JVM flags, using GraalVM native image for millisecond startup, profiling startup with -XX:StartFlightRecording, identifying slow auto-configurations and excluding unnecessary ones, deferring bean initialization using @Lazy, using @ComponentScan with specific packages instead of broad scanning, optimizing database connection pool initialization, implementing async initialization for non-critical components, using Spring Boot 3 ahead-of-time compilation, measuring startup phases and identifying bottlenecks, configuring Hikari pool for faster startup, and testing cold start vs warm start scenarios in containers.

title: Multi-Module Monolith Architecture
question: Design a multi-module Spring Boot monolith with strong module boundaries. Requirements: 1) Clear module separation (order, payment, inventory, user), 2) Enforce compilation-time boundaries, 3) Independent module testing, 4) Shared infrastructure modules, 5) Future microservices extraction path. Discuss: creating Maven multi-module project with parent POM, defining module dependencies in pom.xml with strict visibility rules, using Spring Modulith to enforce module boundaries, implementing package-private visibility for internal classes, using @Configuration per module with component scanning limited to module package, implementing module-specific events for inter-module communication, using ApplicationEventPublisher for decoupled communication, defining module APIs through interfaces in separate API modules, implementing hexagonal architecture within each module, using ArchUnit to enforce architecture rules in tests, creating shared infrastructure module for common utilities, implementing module-specific database schemas with separate repositories, using @Transactional at module boundaries carefully, testing modules independently with @SpringBootTest focused on module, and preparing for microservices split by using event-driven communication patterns.

title: Externalized Configuration Management
question: Implement comprehensive externalized configuration management. Requirements: 1) Support multiple environments (dev, staging, prod), 2) Secrets management without hardcoding, 3) Dynamic configuration updates without restart, 4) Configuration versioning and audit trail, 5) Fallback values for resilience. Discuss: using Spring Cloud Config Server with Git backend for version-controlled configuration, organizing configuration files by profile (application-dev.yml, application-prod.yml), integrating HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager for sensitive data, using @ConfigurationProperties with validation for type-safe configuration, implementing @RefreshScope for runtime configuration updates, using /actuator/refresh endpoint to reload configuration, implementing Spring Cloud Bus with RabbitMQ/Kafka for broadcasting config changes to all instances, encrypting sensitive properties using {cipher} prefix in Config Server, using placeholder default values with ${property:default}, implementing configuration precedence: command line > environment vars > external config > application.yml, creating custom PropertySource for database-driven configuration, implementing configuration change listeners using @EventListener for ConfigFileApplicationListener events, adding audit logging for configuration changes, testing configuration in different environments, and handling configuration failures gracefully with fallback values.

title: Comprehensive Observability Implementation
question: Implement comprehensive observability (metrics, logging, tracing) for a Spring Boot microservice. Requirements: 1) Centralized logging with correlation IDs, 2) Custom business metrics, 3) Distributed tracing across services, 4) Alerting on critical metrics, 5) Performance monitoring. Discuss: integrating Micrometer for metrics with Prometheus registry, exposing /actuator/prometheus endpoint for scraping, creating custom metrics using MeterRegistry with tags for filtering, implementing distributed tracing with Spring Cloud Sleuth (Spring Boot 2) or Micrometer Tracing (Spring Boot 3), integrating Zipkin or Jaeger for trace visualization, configuring sampling rate for traces, implementing structured logging with Logback and JSON format, using MDC to add correlation ID to all logs, generating unique trace ID per request, propagating trace context across service boundaries using HTTP headers, implementing custom log appenders for centralized logging (ELK stack or Loki), creating Grafana dashboards for metrics visualization, setting up Prometheus alerts for high error rates or latency, implementing health indicators for critical dependencies, using @Timed annotation for method-level metrics, creating custom tags for business dimensions, implementing SLI/SLO monitoring, and testing observability in local environment.

title: Implement Resilience Patterns
question: Implement comprehensive resilience patterns for external service calls. Requirements: 1) Circuit breaker for failing services, 2) Retry with exponential backoff, 3) Timeout protection, 4) Bulkhead for thread isolation, 5) Fallback mechanisms, 6) Monitoring and metrics. Discuss: using Resilience4j library with Spring Boot integration, implementing @CircuitBreaker on service methods with failure threshold configuration, configuring circuit breaker states (closed → open → half-open), implementing @Retry with exponential backoff and max attempts, using @TimeLimiter for timeout protection on slow services, implementing @Bulkhead for thread pool isolation to prevent cascading failures, creating fallback methods with same signature for graceful degradation, combining multiple patterns (@Retry + @CircuitBreaker + @TimeLimiter), configuring different resilience patterns per service/endpoint, publishing circuit breaker events to metrics (Micrometer), exposing circuit breaker state via custom health indicators, implementing rate limiting with @RateLimiter to prevent overwhelming services, testing circuit breaker transitions with chaos engineering, using WireMock to simulate failing services in tests, configuring sliding window for failure rate calculation, and monitoring pattern effectiveness with Grafana dashboards.

title: Security Hardening Checklist
question: Implement security hardening for a Spring Boot REST API. Requirements: 1) Secure all endpoints with authentication, 2) Role-based authorization, 3) API rate limiting, 4) Input validation and sanitization, 5) Security headers, 6) Audit logging. Discuss: implementing JWT-based authentication with Spring Security, configuring SecurityFilterChain with role-based authorization rules, using @PreAuthorize and @PostAuthorize for method security, implementing refresh token mechanism for long-lived sessions, enabling HTTPS only with server.ssl configuration and HSTS header, configuring CORS with specific origins instead of wildcards, adding security headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP), implementing rate limiting per user/IP using Bucket4j or Redis, validating all inputs using @Valid and custom validators, sanitizing output to prevent XSS attacks, using parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection, implementing audit logging for security events (login, logout, access denied), encrypting sensitive data at rest using JPA AttributeConverter, configuring session management with proper timeout, implementing CSRF protection for state-changing operations, using Spring Security's password encoders (BCrypt), configuring logout with token invalidation, implementing account lockout after failed attempts, and testing security with OWASP ZAP or Burp Suite.

title: Large-Scale Batch Processing
question: Implement large-scale batch processing system using Spring Batch. Requirements: 1) Process millions of records daily, 2) Fault tolerance and restart capability, 3) Parallel processing, 4) Progress monitoring, 5) Error handling and reporting. Discuss: using Spring Batch with JobRepository for tracking execution state, implementing chunk-oriented processing with ItemReader, ItemProcessor, ItemWriter, configuring optimal chunk size based on transaction overhead and memory, using JpaPagingItemReader or JdbcCursorItemReader for efficient database reading, implementing parallel processing with multi-threading or partitioning, using TaskExecutor for parallel chunk processing, implementing step partitioning for distributed processing, configuring skip policy for non-fatal errors, using ItemProcessListener to track processing progress, implementing retry logic for transient failures, persisting failed items to error table for later reprocessing, using JobParameters to track different executions, implementing restart capability from last successful checkpoint, exposing batch metrics via Actuator custom endpoints, creating scheduled jobs using @Scheduled with proper locking (ShedLock), implementing batch completion notifications, monitoring job execution time and throughput, and testing with different data volumes.
